mbm-1151.clue: I keep a wool radish on my keys.
mbm-1151.quote: I crocheted a whole bunch of radishes for my sister’s pretend shop. One came out barely bigger than my thumb. I bought it with a button and take it everywhere.

mbm-1152.clue: I can read a route by its chalk marks.
mbm-1152.quote: My friend and I worked on a climbing problem all winter. The hold we both feared collected a white halo. The day I got past it, I brushed it clean for the next person.

mbm-1153.clue: I like the museum’s broken things.
mbm-1153.quote: A display of shipwreck crockery held half a plate with a blue rabbit on it. At the museum workshop, I sketched the friend who’d been just out of sight. Then I painted the pair on a practice piece.

mbm-1154.clue: I made a tiny train that runs late.
mbm-1154.quote: My little computer program sends a pixel train around the edge of the screen. I added a station cat that sometimes sleeps on the rails. The conductor waits patiently, just like I meant him to.

mbm-1155.clue: My favorite shop has one customer at a time.
mbm-1155.quote: I visit a market stall built inside an old telephone booth. The owner can sell me a postcard and wind my watch without either of us moving a foot. The best prints hang right under a brass lamp.

mbm-1156.quote: At our Sunday bocce game the red ball and the green ball looked equally close to the little white one. My uncle handed me the measuring string like a judge’s robe. We measured twice, called it a tie and gave the string its own chair.

mbm-1157.clue: I write the little parts first.
mbm-1157.quote: My story began with a crossing guard who only had one line. I gave her an enormous red umbrella. Three chapters later she was the person everybody followed through the rain.

mbm-1158.quote: We spread our board game on the living-room rug and the cat sits on the score pad. We’ve learned to slide her a fresh scrap of paper before each round. She supervises without surrendering her seat.

mbm-1159.clue: I buy a stamp at every museum.
mbm-1159.quote: I press the entry stamp into a paper accordion I made from one long strip. Unfold it and a blue shell sits beside a red bicycle wheel beside a green stone axe. It’s my own tiny gallery.

mbm-1160.clue: I knocked on a suitcase for our first song.
mbm-1160.quote: Our drummer had no kit at our first gig, so I set down my uncle’s old hard case. The latch rattles on the last beat. We book the case for every anniversary show.

mbm-1161.clue: I know where the marimba smiles.
mbm-1161.quote: One wooden bar has a pale curl in the grain like a little grin. My father tapped that note to start my first lesson. Now I touch it lightly even when our tune begins somewhere else.

mbm-1162.clue: I brought the field home in my pocket.
mbm-1162.quote: From my open parachute the fields looked like scraps of brown and green paper. After landing I made a patchwork map from my lunch wrappers. It smells faintly of peanut butter at the landing spot.

mbm-1163.clue: I built the little bicycle first.
mbm-1163.quote: The mecha in my model scene is huge, but I spent three evenings bending wire spokes for a bicycle at its feet. My neighbor spotted it immediately and asked whether the giant paid for parking.

mbm-1164.clue: I can hear my putter cover.
mbm-1164.quote: Mum sewed a tiny brass bell inside my golf cover when I kept leaving it behind. Now my bag gives a little jingle at every hill. Once I even remembered the cover without the bell.

mbm-1165.clue: I played the mayor for exactly eight seconds.
mbm-1165.quote: I had to walk on, snip a paper ribbon and leave. On closing night I found a tiny pair of gold-painted scissors in my pocket. The rest of the cast knew my whole part by heart.

mbm-1166.clue: I keep the club’s ugliest drawing.
mbm-1166.quote: We each had half a minute to sketch a horse from an anime race. Mine had an alarming number of knees. We pinned it beside the television and let it cheer at every race after that.

mbm-1167.clue: I bring a striped scarf to the studio.
mbm-1167.quote: I modeled in my old corduroy suit with the scarf stretched between my hands. Some artists drew the stripes perfectly straight and some made them ripple. I could tell when I’d started laughing by their drawings.

mbm-1168.quote: From one corner of our beach volleyball court the lighthouse sits directly behind the net. I aim just above its red cap. It looks as though the keeper is heading the ball back to shore.

mbm-1169.clue: I fixed a squeak in three lines.
mbm-1169.quote: I wrote a little music program and one note squealed like our gate hinge. Instead of erasing it completely I saved the squeak for the moment a cartoon door swings open. My dad recognized our house.

mbm-1170.clue: I read the city through its mail slots.
mbm-1170.quote: I walked an unfamiliar street looking at the brass slots in old doors. One was shaped like a swallow’s open beak. I sent home a drawing on a postcard and hoped our box was hungry.

mbm-1171.clue: I’ll pedal out of my way for a stone bridge.
mbm-1171.quote: On my canal ride I found a bridge so narrow the handlebars nearly touched both walls. I walked the bicycle across, listening to the little bell chime against every seam in the paving.

mbm-1172.clue: I sleep through the scary scenes in comfort.
mbm-1172.quote: I made a pocket in the big TV blanket for my fuzzy slippers. On monster nights my friend keeps borrowing the slippers to use as puppets so the hero can ask somebody sensible for directions.

mbm-1173.clue: I thought the nest was empty.
mbm-1173.quote: I watched a tumble of dry grass under a roof tile for ten quiet minutes. Then three tiny beaks opened at once. I had looked straight at the little family and only seen the roof.

mbm-1174.clue: I can tune up to a refrigerator.
mbm-1174.quote: Our garage fridge hums a steady note. At band rehearsals I tune my bass against it while the others unpack. When it switched off mid-song once, all four of us missed it.

mbm-1175.clue: I traded a triangle for a story.
mbm-1175.quote: Our neighborhood quilting group swapped scraps with a sentence about each one. I got a red triangle from an umbrella that turned inside out on somebody’s first date. It became the brightest roof on my quilt.
